notes: Test efficacy verified empirically: restored main's assets.go and audit_search.go under the new test file and TestCSVExportsSayWhenTheRowLimitCutThemShort fails on all five assertions (no X-Invenqor-Truncated, no X-Invenqor-Row-Limit, old filename, audit metadata [false false]); it passes on HEAD. go vet ./... and the full server test suite pass (exit 0), and the test was run 30x with no flake.

csv_truncation_test.go:105 the audit-entry check orders by occurred_at only. audit.Recorder never sets occurred_at, so it takes DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, which is second-granularity on SQLite - the two exports in this test almost always share a timestamp. It is deterministic today only because SQLite walks idx_audit_logs_time and breaks ties by rowid; adding a `, id` tiebreak would make the assertion order-independent if the suite is ever pointed at Postgres.

assets.go:222 / audit_search.go:345 lookahead sets Limit = filter.Limit+1 and that value goes straight into the SQL LIMIT with no server-side cap, so the worst case grows from 100,000 to 100,001 rows (50,000 to 50,001 for audit). One extra row; no cap or overflow issue.

Behavior change worth knowing about: the console never passes `limit` (web/src/format.ts:104 downloadPath sets no download attribute, and operationsPages.tsx:336/917 pass only the filter params), so any inventory over the 10,000-row default now downloads as invenqor-assets-partial.csv instead of invenqor-assets.csv. That is the intended fix, but downstream automation matching the fixed filename would break.

No CORS middleware exists in the server, so the new X-Invenqor-* headers need no Access-Control-Expose-Headers; they are only read same-origin. No auth, permission, migration, or deletion logic touched, and the change is a pure code revert - nothing external to undo.
